chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed and Muhammad ibn Khalid, altogether from Al-Qasim ibn Urwa, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, from his father, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

When a prayer is missed by you and you remember it during the time of another [prayer], if you know that if you were to pray the missed one, you would still be within the time [of the current one], then begin with the one that was missed, for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'Establish the prayer for My remembrance.'
And if you know that if you were to pray the one that was missed, the one after it would be missed, then begin with the one whose time you are currently in, so pray it, then establish the other one.
ai.seo_question: What is the correct order for praying missed prayers when their times overlap?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes a pragmatic legal principle for resolving overlapping prayer times, prioritizing the preservation of the current prayer's time over the missed one if necessary. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on balancing the obligation of timely worship (adā) with the duty of making up missed obligations (qadā), ensuring that neither is neglected due to logistical conflict. The ruling underscores the practical application of Quranic injunctions to 'establish prayer' by adapting to human circumstances like sleep or forgetfulness.
